messages:
emma: Hi all, day 1 blocker 44b. Bootstrapped our dotfiles but hitting weird PATH/runtime conflicts: asdf shims not resolving, pnpm missing, and node installed by Volta shows up instead of asdf node. Machine is M1 Mac but corporate image had Rosetta and some older /usr/local bits. Any quick triage?

max: welcome! :tada: We try to standardize on asdf for both python/node. Volta/nvm can conflict. First run `which node` and `which volta`/`volta --version`. Also `echo $PATH` and `cat ~/.tool-versions`.

emma: `which node` -> /Users/emma/.volta/bin/node, `volta --version` -> 1.1.x. `asdf current` prints nothing, `which asdf` -> /opt/homebrew/bin/asdf. My ~/.zshrc is symlinked from dotfiles and has `export PATH="$HOME/.asdf/bin:$PATH"` but not sourcing asdf.sh.

tay: ok two things: 1) If Volta is present it will take precedence; uninstall Volta or disable it if you want asdf. 2) Add asdf sourcing lines near the top of zshrc: `. $(brew --prefix asdf)/libexec/asdf.sh` and `. $(brew --prefix asdf)/etc/profile.d/asdf.sh` then ensure `export PATH="$HOME/.asdf/bin:$PATH"` appears after those lines.

emma: uninstalled Volta via `volta uninstall` and removed its PATH entry. Added the asdf lines and restarted iTerm. `asdf plugin-list` shows python and nodejs, but `asdf install nodejs 18.17.0` fails with gpg key import errors on nodejs plugin.

max: the nodejs asdf plugin requires gpg to verify node dist keys. Install `gpg` via brew then run the plugin's import script: `bash ~/.asdf/plugins/nodejs/bin/import-release-team-keyring` then `asdf install nodejs 18.17.0`.

emma: installed gpg and ran the import script, node install succeeded. For python `asdf install python 3.10.12` failed with a linker error referencing openssl.

tay: brew install openssl readline xz zlib then export build flags before the install: `export LDFLAGS="-L$(brew --prefix openssl)/lib"` and `export CPPFLAGS="-I$(brew --prefix openssl)/include"` then `asdf install python 3.10.12`. For M1 you may see `/opt/homebrew` prefix; that's OK.

emma: brew prefix returns /opt/homebrew. One more quirk: corporate MDM has installers gated so I couldn't symlink to /usr/local before. Could that cause leftover /usr/local files that shadow things?

max: yes, MDM and Rosetta installs can leave stale binaries in /usr/local/bin. Run `ls -l /usr/local/bin | grep pnpm` and remove stale entries (or ask IT). Also `brew doctor` can surface stale files. Using `$(brew --prefix ...)` in dotfiles helps avoid hardcoding.

emma: fixed stale pnpm in /usr/local, reinstalled pnpm with `npm config set prefix "$HOME/.npm-global"` and `npm i -g pnpm`, then added `export PATH="$HOME/.npm-global/bin:$PATH"` to zshrc. `which pnpm` -> ~/.npm-global/bin/pnpm. asdf current shows node 18.17.0 and python 3.10.12. All good.

infra-bot: Created ticket INF-940: "onboarding: note Volta conflict + corporate MDM leftover /usr/local bins in dotfiles README" assigned to @max.

emma: thanks everyone 64c Im going to open a tiny PR to mention Volta and gpg step for nodejs plugin.
